risks: AntigravityAdapter._dispatch() | medium | Returns 'unavailable' with reason 'not_authenticated' when signed_in=False, but does not check if agy is actually signed in; the docstring says 'Nothing here probes it, because probing means invoking a model.' This is by design but could lead to silent failure if signed_in is incorrectly set. | To settle: verify that the signed_in flag is set correctly by the operator in production.

AntigravityAdapter._dispatch() | low | The error handling for 'command not found' checks both 'command not found' and 'not recognized as' in the blob, but the docstring of the class mentions that agy has not completed sign-in; the error handling may mask sign-in issues. | To settle: ensure that the error messages from agy are distinguishable from sign-in issues.

symbols.name: _auth_failure
symbols.note: Returns 'not_authenticated' if result.returncode is not 0 or None and stderr/stdout looks unauthenticated, else empty string.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter
symbols.note: Adapter for Google/Antigravity via SSH. Disabled by default unless signed_in=True. Uses subprocess to run ssh with agy.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter.__init__
symbols.note: Constructor: sets ssh_target, effort, signed_in, ssh_command, _runner, endpoint. Default runner is run_managed. Sets lane to 'untrusted' if not provided.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter.argv
symbols.note: Returns command line list for SSH to run agy with prompt from stdin. Includes -T, BatchMode=yes, ConnectTimeout=5, StrictHostKeyChecking=yes.

symbols.name: AntigravityAdapter._dispatch
symbols.note: Executes the model via subprocess. Returns dict with status, reason, stderr, content, usage. Handles spawn errors, timeout, unauthenticated, connection failures, not_on_path, nonzero exit, bad_response, and success.

claims.text: The prompt goes on STDIN (``agy -p -``) and NEVER on a command line.
claims.why: The argv method constructs a command that includes 'agy', '-p', '-', and the model is passed via --model. The prompt is not on the command line; it is sent via stdin_text in _dispatch.

claims.text: ``ssh`` with a trailing command does not take an argv: it concatenates its arguments and hands the string to the REMOTE login shell, which re-parses it.
claims.why: The argv method constructs a list that ends with '--' and then the remote command. This is consistent with the described behavior.

claims.text: The prompt here is a diff written by a candidate model, so an ordinary patch containing backticks or ``$(...)`` would execute on the bench as Administrator.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the code that generates or passes the prompt. It only shows that the prompt is sent via stdin. The claim about execution is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: This adapter is DISABLED BY DEFAULT: it reports ``unavailable`` / ``not_authenticated`` immediately rather than hanging on an auth prompt.
claims.why: _dispatch checks self.signed_in; if False, returns status 'unavailable' with reason 'not_authenticated'.

claims.text: An operator asserts sign-in with ``signed_in=True``; nothing here probes it, because probing means invoking a model.
claims.why: The __init__ accepts signed_in parameter and _dispatch only checks its value, does not probe actual authentication.

claims.text: The host is passed EXPLICITLY per call.  ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is never read for routing and never written.
